A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same work and contain readable main text, figures, tables, equations, references, and Appendices A–B. All 19 pages were compared through text extraction and rendering.

before.justification: V3 reports original language-model pretraining and fine-tuning experiments in Section 4, a precision ablation in Appendix A.3, and optimization simulations in Appendix B.

after.justification: V4 retains the original pretraining, fine-tuning, precision-ablation, and optimization-simulation results reported in Section 4 and Appendices A–B.

M1.justification: The optimizer procedures, token-half-life scaling rule, model architectures, and memory-efficient fine-tuning approach are unchanged.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same FineWeb-Edu, FineWeb, C4, and MATH coverage, together with the same toy optimization scenario in Appendix B.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is unchanged in every experiment. Removing the duplicate Muon legend entry in Figure 1a does not remove Muon or any other evaluated comparator.

E3.justification: Training budgets, batch sizes, model configurations, hyperparameter searches, precision settings, metrics, and evaluation procedures match throughout Section 4 and the appendices.

E4.justification: The hyperparameter sensitivity analyses, scaling-rule comparisons, stochastic-rounding ablation in Figure 9, and momentum simulation in Figure 10 are unchanged.

E5.justification: Run information and uncertainty reporting are unchanged, including Figure 10's 50% interquartile ranges across random seeds and the uncertainty displays in Figure 8.

E6.justification: Numerical results, plotted curves, rankings, and reported findings match, including the appendices. Figure 1a changes only its legend; its plotted data are identical.

T1.justification: The moment-half-life definition, optimizer equations, scaling relation in Equation (2), and toy loss and noise specification in Appendix B are unchanged.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and Section 5 retain identical claims about small-batch stability, hyperparameter robustness, competitive vanilla SGD, gradient accumulation, and memory-efficient fine-tuning.

C2.justification: The step-size and momentum explanations, throughput and communication qualifications, stochastic-rounding discussion, and remaining open questions are identical.

D1.justification: Appendix A retains the same architecture specifications, learning-rate schedules, precision details, hardware, and computational-cost information. The code-access statement is also unchanged.

R1.justification: Section 3 and all 83 references are unchanged, preserving the same research positioning and relationships to prior work.

P1.justification: The marginal arXiv stamp changes from v3 dated 23 October 2025 to v4 dated 15 December 2025. The prose, headings, and document organization are unchanged.

P2.justification: Figure 1a's legend changes from five entries, including Muon twice, to four entries with Muon once; the legend box becomes shorter. Other figures, tables, captions, and page arrangements are unchanged.

improvement.justification: V4 removes the erroneous duplicate Muon entry from Figure 1a, making the legend clearer and consistent with the four optimizers named in its caption. This is a limited presentation improvement; the scientific evidence and conclusions, including the appendices, are unchanged.
